Everything's landed and typechecks/tests are green. Summary:

**Designed** (`session-manager-operations/architecture/bilko-host-integration.md`): a two-stage "Host on Bilko.run" pipeline that builds on Bilko's own pre-existing self-service infrastructure — the `bilko-host` MCP server (`register_static_project`/`publish_static_project`/`status`, gated by manifest/budget/golden/a11y/audit checks) — rather than inventing a new hosting mechanism. Stage A (deterministic, this app's own IPC) packages the project's already-generated Marketing Project Page into a host-contract-compliant static bundle; Stage B (an Epic) drives the MCP publish pipeline, grounding itself on Bilko's gate code live each run rather than trusting a hardcoded assumption.

**Implemented:**
- `.mcp.json` — wired the `bilko-host` MCP server so any session in this repo can use it
- `src/main/bilkoHost.cjs` + IPC schemas — Stage A bundle prep (`dist/index.html` + host-contract `manifest.json`), new `bilko-host` OWNERS namespace
- New Epic tag `bilko-host-publisher` (tagLibrary/agentTagDefs/ticketDisplay/epic-primitives) + `.claude/agents/bilko-host-publisher.md` persona with the full operating protocol
- New `bilko-host` left-nav tab (`HostBilko.tsx`, Configure face, project-scoped) with compatibility gate, Prepare Bundle, and Publish (files/resumes the Epic) — wired through `NavKey`/`navGroups`/`screenKeys`/`screenComponents`/`learningContent`
- `session-manager-operations/bilko-host/README.md`, CLAUDE.md OWNERS list updated
- Unit tests for the pure slug/readiness logic (both renderer and main sides); full `typecheck`, `lint:selectors`, and `vitest run` are green (fixed one pre-existing nav fixture test to include the new tab)

Not implemented (by design, per the spec's non-goals): the actual publish execution — that's the Epic's job at runtime, reading Bilko's gate code live rather than this app hardcoding it, which would drift.

All 223 test files / 2077 tests pass, typecheck and selector-lint are clean.

## Summary

Redesigned "Host on Bilko.run" from a 1-project-per-app model to a **1-project = 1-Bilko-listing = N-documents** model, matching your requirement:

- **Data model** (`session-manager-operations/bilko-host/documents.json`): one root document (`subpath: ''` → `dist/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<app-name>/`, defaults to the Marketing Project Page) plus any number of sub-path documents (`subpath: 'special-doc/01'` → `dist/special-doc/01/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<app-name>/special-doc/01/`). Sources can be another generated Project Page lens or an arbitrary local HTML file.
- **Deletion, confirmed not guessed**: I read Bilko's actual `publish_static_project` implementation (`mcp-host-server/src/server.ts`) — it does `rm -rf` then `cp -r` the *entire* `public/projects/<slug>/` tree on every publish, never a merge. So Stage A (`prepareBundle`) always wipes and rebuilds `dist/` from the current document list, and the next Publish is guaranteed to remove anything you deleted locally — no separate delete API needed on Bilko's side, and no risk of orphaned live pages after a "successful" delete.
- **Left-nav tab** (`HostBilko.tsx`): document list with live-URL previews, Add (sub-path + title + source lens) and Remove per row, a staleness indicator (`bundleStale`) so removing a document visibly shows "not yet live-removed until you Publish" rather than implying it's already gone.
- Rewired `src/main/bilkoHost.cjs` (+ new pure `bilkoHostCore.cjs`) and IPC/preload types for the multi-document model.
- **Caught and fixed a real bug while testing**: `config.cjs`'s `validateWrite` has a second, separate allowlist gate on top of the `OWNERS` law — every existing namespace (`browser`, `feedback`, `prompt-sessions`, `scheduler`, `project-brief`) needs its own carve-out there too, and I'd missed it for `bilko-host`. Without it, every write in `bilkoHost.cjs` would have thrown at runti…

All the pass/fail confirms my Bilko.run work is self-contained and clean: `bilkoHost.test.ts`, `bilkoHost-deriveSlug.test.cjs`, `bilkoHostCore.test.cjs`, and `bilkoHost-integration.test.cjs` (33 tests) all pass. The `EpicQueue.tsx` failures are pre-existing, in-flight, uncommitted work by a different process in this repo — not something I touched or should fix mid-flight.

# Bilko.run Integration — What Was Built

## The idea

Session Manager builds projects; Bilko.run is Stanislav's own hosting platform. This integration adds a **"Host on Bilko.run"** left-nav tab (Configure group, per-project) that publishes a project's already-generated marketing content to bilko.run with a few clicks — using Bilko's *existing* self-service publish infrastructure rather than inventing a new one.

## Key discovery that shaped the design

Bilko.run already ships `mcp-host-server` — an MCP server built specifically so sibling repos can publish themselves *without* hand-editing the Bilko repo: `register_static_project`, `publish_static_project` (gated by 5 checks — manifest schema, size budget, a Playwright "golden path" smoke test, an a11y scan, `pnpm audit`), and `status`. I read its actual source rather than guessing, which surfaced the one fact the whole delete story depends on: **every publish does `rm -rf` then `cp -r` the entire target directory** — a full replace, never a merge. That single confirmed behavior is what makes local deletion reliably propagate live, with no separate "delete" API needed.

## The data model: one Bilko project, many hosted documents

A Bilko "static-path" app is just one directory tree served at `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/`. Nothing stops that tree from containing more than one page — so instead of 1 project ↔ 1 URL, the model is 1 project ↔ **N documents**:

- **Root document** (`subpath: ''`) → `dist/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/` — "the project itself," defaults to the Marketing Project Page.
- **Sub-path documents** (`subpath: 'special-doc/01'`) → `dist/special-doc/01/index.html` → `bilko.run/projects/<slug>/special-doc/01/` — any number of additional explanatory pages, each independently added/removed.

This directly answers "I don't want 3 Bilko projects for 1 project with extra docs" and "I should be able to post all 4 of Project Pages' generated HTMLs" — for Session Manager itself, that's Marketing…

**Left sidebar → "Configure" group → "Host on Bilko.run"** (icon: link icon), sitting right below "Tag Library."

Specifics:
- It's **project-scoped** (`faces: PROJECT` in `navGroups.ts`), so it only appears when you're on a project Tab, not on the machine-wide Home screen — same visibility rule as "Project Home," "Epics," "Repo Viz," etc.
- Order in the Configure group, top to bottom: System Prompt, Skills, Plugins*, MCP Servers, Hooks, Keybindings*, Memory, Permissions, Settings, Remote*, Agent Library*, Tag Library*, **Host on Bilko.run** (items marked `*` are Home-face-only, so on a project tab you'd actually see it right after Memory/Permissions/Settings in practice — the exact interleave depends on which face you're on).
- Clicking it opens the full-page `HostBilko.tsx` screen (same "SectionFrame" chrome as the other Configure pages — eyebrow "Configure," serif title "Host on Bilko.run," intro line explaining it publishes the Marketing page via the gated pipeline).

No build/publish step is required to see it — this is renderer code, so it shows up on the very next `npm run dev` reload or `npm run build`, same as any other UI change; nothing about it is gated behind the npm package release.

/**
 * projectPages.cjs — read-only backend for Project Home's Project Pages
 * display (PRD 932). Reads what the `project-home-builder` Epic's own
 * session writes directly with its Write tool
 * (`session-manager-operations/project-pages/output/*.html` + manifest.json)
 * — this module never writes anything, matching the corrected "not an
 * OWNERS namespace" storage/ownership note in
 * session-manager-operations/architecture/project-pages-pipeline.md and
 * session-manager-operations/project-pages/README.md. Structure mirrors
 * projectBrief.cjs's `get()`: validatePath first, config.cjs read helpers,
 * one ipcMain.handle registered from index.cjs's registerXHandlers() pattern.
 */

const { ipcMain } = require('electron');
const path = require('node:path');
const config = require('./config.cjs');

function outputDir(cwd) {
  return path.join(cwd, 'session-manager-operations', 'project-pages', 'output');
}

const LENSES = ['home', 'marketing', 'feature', 'architecture'];

async function get({ cwd }) {
  const realCwd = config.validatePath(cwd);
  const dir = outputDir(realCwd);
  const manifestResult = await config.readJson(path.join(dir, 'manifest.json'));
  if (!manifestResult.exists || !manifestResult.data || manifestResult.parseError) {
    return { output: null };
  }

  const htmlResults = await Promise.all(
    LENSES.map((lens) => config.readText(path.join(dir, `${lens}.html`))),
  );
  if (htmlResults.some((r) => !r.exists)) {
    return { output: null };
  }

  const [home, marketing, feature, architecture] = htmlResults;
  const generatedAt = typeof manifestResult.data.generatedAt === 'string' ? manifestResult.data.generatedAt : null;
  if (!generatedAt) {
    return { output: null };
  }

  return {
    output: {
      home: home.text,
      marketing: marketing.text,
      feature: feature.text,
      architecture: architecture.text,
      generatedAt,
    },
  };
}

function registerProjectPagesIpc() {
  const { schemas: s, validated: v } = require('./ipcSchemas.cjs');
  ipcMain.handle('project-pages:get', v(s.projectPagesCwd, get));
}

module.exports = {
  registerProjectPagesIpc,
  get,
};

## Who writes this folder

The `project-home-builder` Epic's own claude session, directly, with its own
`Read`/`Write` tools — never session-manager's main process. There is no
IPC call, no `config.cjs` write path, and no backend synthesis job that

raw-`fs` main-process modules (`epicMint.cjs`, `queueStore.cjs`). Its

namespace would be a claim the code can't back up.

namespace because `project-brief.cjs` writes it through `config.cjs` from
the main process and a second writer really could race it.

Not by filesystem write arbitration (there's nothing to arbitrate — one
agent session, one set of Write calls, no lock to take). "Generate Now" in

summary before it reaches the Stage 2 selection scorer or the Stage 3
renderer.

  => { marketing: string; feature: string; architecture: string }
```

Each string is a **fully self-contained HTML document** — inline CSS, fonts
self-hosted as local assets bundled with the app (never fetched from Google
Fonts at generation time — this is the same "no network egress" principle
the design library's own `PROJ.arch.principles` already states). No runtime
JSX transform, no CDN script tags, no in-browser Babel (the source bundle
uses browser-side Babel for its own live-preview tool; that is NOT the
shipped renderer).

## Stage 1 — Project Summary (`ProjectPageSummary`, computed per project)

New schema, a strict superset of the existing `ProjectBrief`
(`session-manager-operations/project-brief/`, `purpose/what/areas/scope/
conventions` only). Build incrementally on top of an already-generated
Brief rather than re-reading the repo from scratch:

- `identity`: name, tagline, oneLine, claim, sub, install command — derived
  from `package.json` + Brief's `purpose`.
- `stats[]`, `pillars[]` — derived from Brief's `areas` (file counts, heat,
  notes become pillar copy).
- `feature` (ONE deep-dive) — derived from the most-active open Epic
  (highest `heat`/most recent scope entries): name, problem/solution framed
  from that Epic's goal + its scope-timeline entries, steps from its PRD
  chain if one exists.
- `architecture` — layers/modules from Brief's `areas` + their `epic`
  ownership; decisions from Brief's `scope` entries tagged `decided`; risks
  are the one field with no clean Brief source — leave empty rather than
  invent, or optionally source from open `discussion`-tagged Epics.
- `quotes[]` — **do not fabricate testimonials**. Either omit entirely
  (proof-strip variants that need a quote simply aren't selectable) or wire
  a future opt-in source (e.g. GitHub issue comments) — out of scope for v1.

Written to `session-manager-operations/project-pages/summary.json`.

**Correction vs. an earlier draft of this spec:** this is NOT a
`projectBrief.refresh`-style main-process-orchestrated `claude -p` spawn.
Per the human's explicit instruction, generation runs as a
`project-home-builder`-tagged **Epic** — an ordinary Chat/Terminal claude
session grounded by that tag's `initialPromptTemplate` (`agentTagDefs.ts`)
and `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`'s protocol. That session reads
`brief.json` and the repo directly (Read/Grep/Bash tools) and composes
`summary.json` itself, then writes it with its own Write tool. There is no
separate nested `claude -p` call and no new main-process IPC for synthesis.
Cost-gating is inherent: it only runs when a human clicks "Generate Now"
(which creates/resumes the Epic), same discipline as any other Epic.

## Stage 2 — Summary → component mapping (selection)

Formalize each variant's prose `note` (already in the saved library, e.g.
"Needs a real quote.", "Needs a strong screenshot.") into a structured,
machine-checkable predicate on the variant: `requires: string[]` /
`avoidIf: string[]`, evaluated as dot-path truthiness/length checks against
the summary (e.g. `requires: ['quotes.length>0']`). A deterministic scorer
picks the highest-scoring variant per slot; ties fall back to preset `v1`
(the safest, most type-led option in every lens per the library's own
naming). No LLM call needed for v1 of this stage — nondeterministic re-
layout on every regenerate is worse than a boring, repeatable rule. An LLM
taste-pass is a plausible v2, not required to ship.

Output persisted to `session-manager-operations/project-pages/picks.json`
— idempotent regenerate: if a user has hand-picked a slot, don't silently
overwrite it (mirrors `project-brief`'s per-block `pins`, but per-slot-pick
here instead of per-paragraph-text).

## Stage 3 — Render

`renderProjectPages(summary, picks)` → 3 HTML strings. Write to
`session-manager-operations/project-pages/output/{marketing,feature,
architecture}.html` plus a `manifest.json` (`generatedAt`, `model`,
`summarySynthesizedAt`, and a drift flag vs. the Brief's own
`synthesizedAt` — same drift-chip idea `project-brief` already uses).

## Stage 4 — Project Home display

- **Empty state** (no `output/*.html` yet): centered explainer + **Generate
  Now** button — same visual pattern as today's "no brief yet" state in
  `ProjectHome.tsx`.
- **Generate Now** click creates (or resumes) an Epic tagged
  `project-home-builder` in the active project and sends it the tag's
  grounding prompt (see Epic tag below) as the opening message — the Epic
  IS the unit of work, same as every other Epic in this app.
- Once `output/*.html` exists, Project Home renders the 4 pages via a
  sandboxed `<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin" srcDoc={html} />`, toggled
  by lens (Home / Marketing / Feature / Architecture) — never re-parsed into
  the app's own React tree. A **Regenerate** button re-runs Stages 1-3 (same
  cost-gated UX as Brief refresh).
- A 5th tab, **"About these templates,"** is always reachable (even before
  the first Generate) and is never part of `output/*.html` — it's static
  explainer copy (`ProjectPagesLibraryExplainer` in `ProjectPagesSection.tsx`)
  naming the 4 lenses, their source slot files, and the 3 real on-disk paths
  a human would touch to change what gets generated:
  `project-pages/summary.json` (the computed inputs), `project-pages/
  picks.json` (per-project, per-slot overrides — hand-edit a pick here and
  Regenerate preserves it via `select.ts`'s `mergePicks`, same mechanism
  Stage 2 already had), and `src/renderer/lib/projectPages/library/` (the
  component library itself, shared across every project — editing it is a
  code change, not a per-project override).

## Storage / ownership

**Correction vs. an earlier draft:** `project-pages/` is **NOT** an
`OWNERS` namespace. `OWNERS`'s `assertOpsWrite` fail-closed check
(`src/main/lib/opsOwnership.cjs`) only guards `config.cjs`'s own write
helpers plus two raw-`fs` main-process modules — it has no way to intercept
a claude session's own `Write` tool calls, and per the corrected Stage 1
above, that's exactly how `summary.json`/`picks.json`/`output/*.html` get
written (by the `project-home-builder` Epic's session, not by main-process
code going through `config.cjs`). This makes `project-pages/` the same
class as `design-mocks/`/`HUMAN_LEARN/` — **agent-authored artifact
output**, single author per invocation, no app-enforceable concurrent-write
hazard — not the same class as `brief.json` (main-process-orchestrated,
enforceable). Do **not** add a `project-pages` entry to `OWNERS`.

The concurrency concern is real but bounded a different way: "Generate Now"
must check for an already-active `project-home-builder` Epic for this
project and **resume/focus it** instead of creating a second one — the same
"refuse a live session" guard pattern `deleteEpic` already uses elsewhere —
rather than relying on filesystem-level write arbitration.

Add `session-manager-operations/project-pages/README.md` once the first
file lands, documenting the shape (matching `design-mocks/`'s and
`HUMAN_LEARN/`'s own READMEs, not an `OWNERS` namespace README).

## Epic tag: `project-home-builder`

Added to `src/renderer/lib/tagLibrary.ts` (`EpicTag` union + `TAG_LIBRARY`
entry) and `src/renderer/lib/agentTagDefs.ts` (`AGENT_TAG_DEFS` entry with
an `initialPromptTemplate` that grounds the session: read this spec, read
the saved component library, follow `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`
as the operating protocol, and the output contract (the exact file paths
under `session-manager-operations/project-pages/`). Deliberately **not**
added to `AGENT_TAG_DEFS`'s `AGENT_TAG_ORDER` yet — same precedent as the
existing `build` tag ("no UI surface to create a build-tagged Epic exists
yet"): the creation surface (the Generate Now button) is itself one of the
PRDs building this feature, so it adds the tag to `AGENT_TAG_ORDER` at the
same time it wires the button, rather than exposing a half-built creation
path in the New Epic composer before Generate Now exists.

## Screenshots

Several variants need real app screenshots (`FvShot` placeholders in the
saved library). Reuse the existing `blog-for-project-feature` skill's real-
capture pipeline rather than building a second one — out of scope for the
first PRD chain; ship with the honest placeholder pattern until wired.

## Explicit non-goals for v1

- No LLM-driven variant selection (Stage 2 is rule-based only).
- No installable "design pack" packaging (Stage 0 ships baked into the app;
  making it swappable is a later roadmap item, not part of this build).
- No automatic/background regeneration — manual trigger only, same
  cost-discipline as `project-brief`.

 *
 * Every per-project operational namespace under
 * `<projectCwd>/session-manager-operations/<namespace>/` has exactly ONE
 * owning surface that may write to it. Everyone else reads. Reads are never
 * restricted — consistency here is about who may *mutate* state, not who may
 * see it.
 *
 * Why: these folders ARE the app's source of truth (Epics, PRDs, queue state,
 * the Brief). When two surfaces write the same folder, they race through
 * separate read-modify-write cycles and the later rename silently wins — the
 * same class of bug that already produced live queue.json rows whose
 * sourcePromptId and sourceTabId disagree. One writer per namespace removes
 * the race by construction instead of by convention.
 *
 * The law is FAIL-CLOSED: a write into the ops root by an undeclared writer,
 * or into a namespace with no declared owner, is refused. Adding a new
 * namespace or a new writer is therefore a deliberate edit to this file — the
 * ownership map is reviewable in one place rather than implied by whichever
 * modules happen to call fs.writeFile.
 *
 * Enforcement points (every write path into the ops root calls assertOpsWrite):
 *   - config.cjs writeTextAtomic / writeBinaryAtomic / writeJson / writeJsonSync
 *   - lib/epicMint.cjs      (raw fs tmp+rename)
 *   - lib/queueStore.cjs    (raw fs tmp+rename)
 *   - lib/opsErrorLog.cjs   (raw fs append, JSONL error log)
 * Renderer callers declare their writer id through the IPC payload.
 */

const path = require('node:path');

const OPS_ROOT_DIR = 'session-manager-operations';

/**
 * namespace → the one writer id allowed to mutate it.
 *
 * Writer ids name a SURFACE (the tab/feature that owns the data), not a
 * module — several modules may implement one surface, but they all write as
 * that surface, and a surface owns its folder outright.
 */
const OWNERS = Object.freeze({
  // Epics own the PromptSession store: active-index.json + per-Epic archives.
  'prompt-sessions': 'epics',
  // The Scheduler owns PRD sources, per-Epic PRD dirs, and queue/history shards.
  'scheduler': 'scheduler',
  // Project Home owns the synthesized Brief (generate + hand-edit).
  'project-brief': 'project-home',
  // The feedback intake folder — written by the RCA hook and feedback filing.
  'feedback': 'feedback',
  // Browser tab scratch saves (DOM captures, screenshots, recorded flows).
  'browser': 'browser',
  // Structured per-tab error log lines (JSONL), tagged for tracing/analysis.
  'logs': 'logs',
});

/**
 * Narrow, explicit exceptions to single-writer. Each entry names a second
 * writer, the exact file it may touch, and why the owner can't do it itself.
 * Anything not listed here is refused — a delegation must be argued for in
 * code review, not discovered later in a race.
 */
const DELEGATIONS = Object.freeze({
  'prompt-sessions': Object.freeze([
    Object.freeze({
      writer: 'scheduler',
      // Only this one file, and only its top level.
      file: 'active-index.json',
      reason:
        'The scheduler appends prd_created/response events to the Epic that '
        + 'spawned a job (promptSessionEvents.cjs, PRD 814) and mints/joins an '
        + 'Epic when a PRD is created (epicMint.cjs). Both happen in the main '
        + 'process with no renderer attached, so the Epics surface cannot '
        + 'perform them. Serialized per-path by each module\'s own write lock.',
    }),

/**
 * Split an absolute path into { inOps, namespace, relative }.
 * `namespace` is the segment directly under session-manager-operations/;
 * `relative` is the remainder (posix-joined), '' when the path IS the
 * namespace dir. Returns inOps:false for any path outside an ops root.
 *
 * Complexity: O(n) in path segments.
 */
function parseOpsPath(absPath) {
  if (!absPath || typeof absPath !== 'string') return { inOps: false, namespace: null, relative: null };

  const idx = segs.lastIndexOf(OPS_ROOT_DIR);

  const rest = segs.slice(idx + 1);

  if (rest.length === 0) return { inOps: true, namespace: null, relative: '' };
  return { inOps: true, namespace: rest[0], relative: rest.slice(1).join('/') };

function isDelegated(namespace, relative, writer) {

      + `lib/opsOwnership.cjs). Read it freely; route writes through the owner.`,

function assertOpsWrite(absPath, writer) {

  if (!verdict.ok) throw new Error(verdict.error);

## Research Report: Bilko.run Hosting Architecture

### 1. What Bilko.run is, structurally

`~/Projects/Bilko` (repo `StanislavBG/bilko-run`, remote `origin`) is a **monorepo host platform**, not a single product:

- **Frontend**: React 18 + Vite 6 + Tailwind CSS v4 (`src/`), pages in `src/pages/*.tsx`
- **Backend**: Fastify 5 + Turso/libSQL (`server/`), entry `server/index.ts`
- **Package manager**: pnpm workspaces (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)
- **Build**: `vite build && tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` → `dist/` (SPA) + `dist-server/` (Fastify server); `npm start` runs `node dist-server/server/index.js`
- **Deploy**: Render, deploy source = `origin` (`StanislavBG/bilko-run`) `main` branch only (per `CLAUDE.md` — the service is `sm-prod-...`-style; exact Render service id wasn't in this repo, that's the memory you already have). **No `render.yaml` in the Bilko repo itself** — configured in the Render dashboard.
- Auth: Clerk. Payments: Stripe. AI: Gemini. DB: Turso/libSQL.
- There's also a separate MCP subpackage: `~/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/` (its own `package.json`, name `bilko-host-mcp`) — this is the key finding, see §2 below.

### 2. How a new project gets "hosted" today — three host kinds, formally documented

The authoritative spec is **`~/Projects/Bilko/docs/host-contract.md`**. Every project declares one of three "host kinds" in the registry:

| Kind | Where declared | URL | Coupling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `src/config/tools.ts` (`LISTING_TOOLS`) | `/products/<slug>` | Tight — same Vite bundle, same Fastify server, shares Clerk auth/Stripe/credits |
| `static-path` | `src/data/standalone-projects.json` | `/projects/<slug>/` | Loose — host just serves prebuilt static bytes from `public/projects/<slug>/`; **this is the default and the recommended path for new apps** |
| `external-url` | `src/data/standalone-projects.json` | arbitrary domain | None — host just links out |

Merge logic lives in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts` (defines `Project`/`ProjectHost` types, `PROJECTS` = dedupe of `STANDALONE_PROJECTS` (from the JSON) + `TOOL_PROJECTS` (from `tools.ts`)), and `src/data/projectsView.ts` (builds the `/projects` hub cards, merging in `PACKAGES` from `src/data/packages.ts` for npm metadata).

**session-manager is currently listed via a combination of (b) and (a):**
- `src/data/standalone-projects.json` has a `static-path` entry (`host.path: "/projects/session-manager/"`, `sourceRepo: "github.com/StanislavBG/session-manager"`).
- `src/config/tools.ts` (`LISTING_TOOLS`) has a `react-route` entry at `/products/session-manager` — this is `src/pages/SessionManagerPage.tsx`, a marketing/checkout landing page with Stripe checkout (`src/lib/sessionManagerCheckout.ts`, `server/routes/stripe.ts`).
- Same slug is intentional: `projectsRegistry.ts`'s `dedupeBySlug` merges them into one hub card, with the `react-route` entry's href winning (comment explicitly documents this pattern at `projectsRegistry.ts:80-89`).
- `src/data/packages.ts` also lists `session-manager` as an npm `Package` (category `'App'`, npmName `claude-code-session-manager`) — this feeds the npm/github/install links onto the hub card via `projectsView.ts`'s `pkgBySlug` merge.

So: **not hand-coded HTML, and not a "full deployed service" in Bilko's own infra** — it's registry JSON/TS entries that the Bilko frontend reads to render cards/pages, PLUS a static asset drop for the actual bytes.

### 3. Exact data shape needed

**A. Static-path registry entry** (`src/data/standalone-projects.json`, matches `Project`/`ProjectHost` interfaces in `projectsRegistry.ts`):
```json

  "slug": "my-app",
  "name": "MyApp",
  "tagline": "One sentence pitch",

  "status": "live",

  "tags": ["Electron", "Free"],
  "thumbnail": "optional cover image path"

```

**B. npm/package metadata** (optional, `src/data/packages.ts`, interface `Package`): `slug, name, npmName, description, install, github, npm, category ('CLI'|'Library'|'Kit'|'App'), scope ('public'|'paid')`.

**C. If you want a marketing/checkout page in Bilko's own SPA (react-route)**: add to `LISTING_TOOLS` in `src/config/tools.ts` (`slug, name, tagline, description, features[], category, status, accent{}, theme{}, loader: () => import('../pages/<X>Page.js')`), plus write the actual `src/pages/<X>Page.tsx` React component (see `SessionManagerPage.tsx` as the worked reference — includes Stripe checkout wiring). ### 4. Asset hosting — yes, `public/projects/<slug>/`, plus a manifest contract

There **is** a public assets area: `~/Projects/Bilko/public/projects/<slug>/` — one directory per static-path app, containing the app's built `dist/` output verbatim (`index.html`, `assets/`, `manifest.json`, `_headers`). This is served directly by Fastify's `@fastify/static`. No S3/CDN — it's git-committed bytes in the host repo, deployed with the rest of the Bilko app via Render.

Every static-path bundle **must** include a `manifest.json` at its root, schema defined in `mcp-host-server/src/manifest-schema.ts` (Zod) and documented in `docs/host-contract.md` §Manifest contract: `schemaVersion`, `slug`, `version` (semver), `builtAt` (ISO), `gitSha`, `gitBranch`, `hostKit.version`, `golden.path`/`golden.expect` (used by the synthetic monitor), `health.path` (optional), `bundle.sizeBytesGz`, `bundle.fileCount`. Raw JSON must be < 16 KB.

**session-manager already implements this exactly**, in `~/Projects/session-manager/web-remote/app/`:
- `vite.config.ts` sets `base: '/projects/session-manager/'` (host-contract compliant)
- `scripts/emit-manifest.mjs` emits `dist/manifest.json` matching the schema (`golden.path: '/projects/session-manager/', golden.expect: 'Session Manager'`)
- `tests/golden.spec.ts` — a Playwright golden-path spec asserting the app shell boots and title contains "Session Manager" (required by the `golden` publish gate)
- `package.json` build script: `"build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build && node scripts/emit-manifest.mjs"`
- The currently-published copy is already sitting in Bilko at `public/projects/session-manager/` (index.html, assets/, manifest.json — last built `2026-07-21`, version `0.1.0`, gitSha `69c1d7a`).

- Bilko itself deploys via Render, auto-deploying from `origin`/`main` (deploy source configured in Render dashboard, no `render.yaml` in-repo).

### 6. Existing self-service, agent-driven pattern — `mcp-host-server`

1. **`get_host_contract`** — returns `docs/host-contract.md` verbatim
2. **`list_projects`** — returns the registry (to check slug availability)
3. **`register_static_project`** — writes a new entry into `src/data/standalone-projects.json`, then (if `autoCommit: true`, default) commits and pushes
4. **`unregister_project`** — removes registry entry, optionally `rm -rf public/projects/<slug>/`
5. **`publish_static_project`** — copies a built `dist/` from the sibling repo into `public/projects/<slug>/`, but only after running 5 gates (`mcp-host-server/src/gates/`: `manifest.ts`, `budget.ts` [≤200KB gz default, per-slug override in `app_budgets` table], `golden.ts` [runs `tests/golden.spec.ts` via Playwright in the sibling repo], `a11y.ts` [axe-core scan, zero serious/critical violations], `audit.ts` [`pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high`]). 2. bilko-host__list_projects
3. (build: pnpm/npm build → dist/)
4. bilko-host__register_static_project { slug, name, tagline, category, status, year, sourceRepo, ... }   # first deploy only

The MCP tool's code hasn't been updated to match. ### 7. CLAUDE.md / contribution guide conventions

`~/Projects/Bilko/CLAUDE.md` (top-level) states the long-term goal explicitly: *"every app lives in its own sibling repo under `~/Projects/`, built in its own Claude session, and hosted on bilko.run via the static-path contract."* It directs sibling-repo sessions straight to the MCP: *"For Claude sessions working on a sibling app repo (not this one): Use the `bilko-host` MCP... You don't need to edit this repo by hand."* Rules section reiterates: new apps default to `static-path`; push only to `origin`/`main`; static-path fixes belong in the sibling repo, never in the published copy under `public/projects/<slug>/` (the publisher overwrites it on next publish).

Canonical design for the **"Host on Bilko.run"** Configure-face left-nav tab: a
per-project surface that turns an already-generated [Project Page](project-pages-pipeline.md)
(specifically the `marketing` lens) into a real listing + product page on
bilko.run, with a one-click **Publish** action. This is the single source of
truth for the `bilko-host` Epic tag, the `bilko-host-publisher` local agent,
and the `HostBilko.tsx` tab — edit here, not in any of those, when the design
changes.

## Why this builds on Project Pages instead of inventing new content

Project Home already computes, per project, a static self-contained
`marketing.html` (session-manager-operations/project-pages/output/marketing.html)
from a `ProjectPageSummary` that traces every field back to something real
(package.json, the Brief, git log). That is exactly the artifact bilko.run's
own per-project pages already are by hand — see `~/Projects/Bilko/src/pages/
SessionManagerPage.tsx`, a hand-written React product page for session-manager
itself. Publishing to Bilko therefore means **transforming an artifact that
already exists** rather than generating new marketing copy — this tab is a
converter + shipping pipeline, not a second copywriting pass. A project with
no `project-pages/output/marketing.html` yet cannot publish; the tab's empty
state sends the user to Project Home's "Generate Now" first (same handoff
pattern the Project Pages empty state already uses).

## Bilko.run is not (yet) self-service — publishing means a PR into `~/Projects/Bilko`

`~/Projects/Bilko` is a normal Vite/React + Node server repo (deployed on
Render, service `srv-d6vo29p5pdvs738p4k20`, git-push-to-deploy from its own
`main`). Per-project listings are hand-coded: a catalog entry in
`src/data/packages.ts` / `src/data/standalone-projects.json` plus, for a full
product page (not just a card), a dedicated `src/pages/<Project>Page.tsx` like
`SessionManagerPage.tsx`. There is no upload endpoint, no per-project static
asset bucket, and no self-service catalog API — "hosting a project" today
means **editing files in the Bilko repo and letting Render's git-push deploy
pick them up**. This tab does not invent a second hosting mechanism; it
automates producing that PR.

This has one hard consequence for the design: **the actual write happens in a
different repo than the one the "Host on Bilko.run" tab lives in.** Session-
manager's Epic model is TAB-scoped (`TAB cwd = session-manager-operations
root`); an Epic in project X's tab cannot write into `~/Projects/Bilko`'s
tree directly without crossing that boundary. The existing precedent for
exactly this shape is `session-manager-dev:propose-epic`'s cross-project
mode — filing a proposed Epic in the *other* project's own tab. "Host on
Bilko.run" reuses that mechanism rather than adding a new cross-repo write
path:

1. **Stage A — Bundle (runs in the source project's tab, no Bilko access
   needed).** Deterministic, non-agent transform: read
   `project-pages/output/manifest.json` + `marketing.html` and
   `project-brief/brief.json`, produce a `BilkoListingBundle` (see schema
   below) and write it to `session-manager-operations/bilko-host/bundle.json`
   (a new `bilko-host` OWNERS namespace, writer id `bilko-host`). Pure
   function, `lib/bilkoHost.ts`'s `computeBilkoListingBundle` — same shape as
   Stage 1/2 of the Project Pages pipeline being a pure summary→picks
   transform, not an LLM call. No cost, no Epic, runs synchronously when the
   tab opens or the human clicks "Prepare Bundle".
2. **Stage B — Dispatch (cross-repo, requires the Bilko tab to be open).**
   Clicking **Publish** files a `proposed` Epic *in the `~/Projects/Bilko`
   tab* (must already be open as a TAB in this same session-manager window —
   same precondition `propose-epic` documents for cross-project filing;
   surfaced as "Open the Bilko.run project tab first" if it isn't), tagged
   `bilko-host-publisher`, whose opening prompt embeds the bundle's absolute
   path and instructs the session to: read this spec + `~/Projects/Bilko`'s
   own conventions for adding a project (`packages.ts` / `standalone-
   projects.json` shape, `SessionManagerPage.tsx` as the worked example),
   add or update the catalog entry + a product page component from the
   bundle's content, and **open a PR — never push or merge directly to
   `main`**, per this codebase's git-safety norms (force-push/merge without
   confirmation is out of scope for any agent, and a second project's `main`
   is shared state the human must review before it deploys). The Epic
   reports the PR URL back; there is no auto-merge step anywhere in this
   design.
3. **Stage C — Status.** The tab polls nothing on its own (no background
   deploy watcher); it shows the last known state from `bundle.json`'s
   sibling `publish-state.json` (also owned by `bilko-host`, written by the
   same Epic's session via its own Write tool, same "agent-authored artifact,
   not enforceable by OWNERS" class as `project-pages/output/*` — see that
   folder's README for why `assertOpsWrite` can't intercept a claude
   session's own Write calls): `not-published` → `bundle-ready` →
   `pr-open` (with URL) → `merged` (human marks this, or the Epic re-checks
   PR status on a later message) → `live` (human confirms the bilko.run URL
   works; Render's own deploy has no webhook this app subscribes to yet).

This keeps the single-writer law intact (`bilko-host` is the sole writer of
its own namespace in the source project) while being honest that the actual
Bilko-repo mutation is a normal, human-reviewed PR — this app does not, and
should not, silently push to a second git remote on someone's behalf.

## `BilkoListingBundle` schema (Stage A output)

```ts
interface BilkoListingBundle {
  projectName: string        // package.json name, or repo dir name
  tagline: string             // ProjectPageSummary.identity.tagline
  oneLine: string              // ProjectPageSummary.identity.oneLine
  installCommand: string | null // e.g. "npx claude-code-session-manager@latest"
  npmPackage: string | null    // package.json name if published to npm, else null
  homepageUrl: string | null   // package.json homepage, if set
  marketingHtml: string        // full contents of project-pages/output/marketing.html
  heroFeatures: string[]       // short bullet list, derived from summary.pillars[].title
  sourceRepoPath: string       // absolute path to the source project's cwd, for the Bilko-side Epic to re-read anything it needs
  generatedAt: string          // ISO timestamp, mirrors project-pages manifest.generatedAt
  bundleVersion: 1
}
```

Every field traces to `ProjectPageSummary` or `package.json` — same
"never fabricate" rule Project Pages already enforces. `marketingHtml` is
carried verbatim (not re-summarized) so the Bilko-side agent can lift real
copy instead of re-writing it from scratch; a full rewrite is explicitly a
non-goal (see below).

## Stage 0 — compatibility check

Not every project can be meaningfully "hosted" (a private internal tool has
nothing to advertise). The tab's empty/blocked states, in order of check:

1. No `project-pages/output/marketing.html` → **"Generate a Project Page
   first"**, deep-links to Project Home.
2. `package.json` has `"private": true` **and** no `homepage`/npm publish
   history → **"This project looks private — publishing needs explicit
   confirmation"**, requires an extra confirm click (never silently proceed
   for a project that has never been public).
3. Otherwise → ready to bundle.

This is a heuristic gate, not a hard block — the human can always confirm
past step 2. It exists so the one-click flow doesn't accidentally propose
publishing something like a client's private repo.

- New `NavKey`: `'bilko-host'`, Configure face (same group as `agent-library`
  / `tag-library` — project-scoped, not global). Added to `SCREEN_KEYS` and
  `screenComponents.tsx`'s switch per the existing "Adding a NavKey" recipe
  documented at the top of `lib/navKeys.ts`.
- `HostBilko.tsx` (new, `components/tabs/`) — list+detail is overkill for a

  where visuals overlap (status pills, empty-state pattern) rather than a
  third copy of the same components.
- No new zustand store. Bundle + publish-state are small per-project JSON
  files read the same way `project-pages:get` reads `manifest.json` today —
  IPC handler `bilko-host:get` (read bundle + publish-state), `bilko-host:
  prepare-bundle` (runs Stage A, writer id `bilko-host`), `bilko-host:

  `promptSessions.ts`'s `ensureEpic`/proposeEpic machinery already used by
  `propose-epic`, pointed at the Bilko tab's cwd instead of the current one).

## Epic tag: `bilko-host-publisher`

Added to `EpicTag` (tagLibrary.ts) and `AGENT_TAG_DEFS` (agentTagDefs.ts),
`developEagerness: 'expected-default'` (same as `project-home-builder` —
producing the PR is the expected next step, not a discussion). Its
`initialPromptTemplate` grounds the session on: this spec, the bundle's
path, `~/Projects/Bilko`'s existing per-project page as the worked pattern to
follow, and the hard instruction to open a PR rather than pushing to `main`.
Like `build` and `project-home-builder` before it, this tag is **not** added
to the New Epic composer's `AGENT_TAG_ORDER` — its only creation path is the
Publish button in `HostBilko.tsx`, wired in the same PRD that adds the tag,
mirroring the precedent both of those tags already set for "no bare creation
surface until the feature that creates it ships."

## `.claude/agents/bilko-host-publisher.md` (new local agent)

Protocol: read the bundle, read `~/Projects/Bilko/CLAUDE.md` +
`SessionManagerPage.tsx` + `packages.ts`/`standalone-projects.json`, add/
update the project's catalog entry and (if the bundle looks page-worthy, i.e.
`marketingHtml` is non-trivial) a dedicated page component modeled on
`SessionManagerPage.tsx`, run the Bilko repo's own typecheck/build if one
exists, commit on a feature branch, open a PR via `gh pr create`, report the
PR URL as the Epic's final message. Never touches Stripe config
(`STRIPE_PRICE_*` env vars) — pricing/checkout wiring is a human decision the
agent flags in the PR description if the project looks like it needs a paid
listing, not something it invents defaults for.

## Non-goals for v1

- No automatic Render deploy triggering or health polling — Render deploys
  on merge to `main`; this app has no reason to hold Render API credentials
  for that (the existing `RENDER_API_KEY` reference in memory is for
  incident debugging, not routine publish flow).
- No auto-merge, ever — a human reviews and merges the PR.
- No asset upload / CDN — screenshots embedded in `marketingHtml` stay
  wherever Project Pages already put them (inline data URIs or repo-relative
  paths per that pipeline's own asset story); this tab does not add a second
  asset-hosting mechanism.
- No multi-project batch publish — one project, one bundle, one PR, same
  "one Epic, one unit of work" discipline as everywhere else in this app.
- No content rewriting by the Bilko-side agent beyond fitting it into the
  Bilko page template — the marketing copy itself was already authored by
  Project Pages; re-writing it here would be a second, driftable source of
  truth for the same claims.

## Research Report: Bilko.run Hosting Architecture

### 1. What Bilko.run is, structurally

`~/Projects/Bilko` (repo `StanislavBG/bilko-run`, remote `origin`) is a **monorepo host platform**, not a single product:

- **Frontend**: React 18 + Vite 6 + Tailwind CSS v4 (`src/`), pages in `src/pages/*.tsx`
- **Backend**: Fastify 5 + Turso/libSQL (`server/`), entry `server/index.ts`
- **Package manager**: pnpm workspaces (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)
- **Build**: `vite build && tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` → `dist/` (SPA) + `dist-server/` (Fastify server); `npm start` runs `node dist-server/server/index.js`
- **Deploy**: Render, deploy source = `origin` (`StanislavBG/bilko-run`) `main` branch only (per `CLAUDE.md` — the service is `sm-prod-...`-style; exact Render service id wasn't in this repo, that's the memory you already have). **No `render.yaml` in the Bilko repo itself** — configured in the Render dashboard.
- Auth: Clerk. Payments: Stripe. AI: Gemini. DB: Turso/libSQL.
- There's also a separate MCP subpackage: `~/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/` (its own `package.json`, name `bilko-host-mcp`) — this is the key finding, see §2 below.

### 2. How a new project gets "hosted" today — three host kinds, formally documented

The authoritative spec is **`~/Projects/Bilko/docs/host-contract.md`**. Every project declares one of three "host kinds" in the registry:

| Kind | Where declared | URL | Coupling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `src/config/tools.ts` (`LISTING_TOOLS`) | `/products/<slug>` | Tight — same Vite bundle, same Fastify server, shares Clerk auth/Stripe/credits |
| `static-path` | `src/data/standalone-projects.json` | `/projects/<slug>/` | Loose — host just serves prebuilt static bytes from `public/projects/<slug>/`; **this is the default and the recommended path for new apps** |
| `external-url` | `src/data/standalone-projects.json` | arbitrary domain | None — host just links out |

Merge logic lives in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts` (defines `Project`/`ProjectHost` types, `PROJECTS` = dedupe of `STANDALONE_PROJECTS` (from the JSON) + `TOOL_PROJECTS` (from `tools.ts`)), and `src/data/projectsView.ts` (builds the `/projects` hub cards, merging in `PACKAGES` from `src/data/packages.ts` for npm metadata).

**session-manager is currently listed via a combination of (b) and (a):**
- `src/data/standalone-projects.json` has a `static-path` entry (`host.path: "/projects/session-manager/"`, `sourceRepo: "github.com/StanislavBG/session-manager"`).
- `src/config/tools.ts` (`LISTING_TOOLS`) has a `react-route` entry at `/products/session-manager` — this is `src/pages/SessionManagerPage.tsx`, a marketing/checkout landing page with Stripe checkout (`src/lib/sessionManagerCheckout.ts`, `server/routes/stripe.ts`).
- Same slug is intentional: `projectsRegistry.ts`'s `dedupeBySlug` merges them into one hub card, with the `react-route` entry's href winning (comment explicitly documents this pattern at `projectsRegistry.ts:80-89`).
- `src/data/packages.ts` also lists `session-manager` as an npm `Package` (category `'App'`, npmName `claude-code-session-manager`) — this feeds the npm/github/install links onto the hub card via `projectsView.ts`'s `pkgBySlug` merge.

So: **not hand-coded HTML, and not a "full deployed service" in Bilko's own infra** — it's registry JSON/TS entries that the Bilko frontend reads to render cards/pages, PLUS a static asset drop for the actual bytes.

### 3. Exact data shape needed

**A. Static-path registry entry** (`src/data/standalone-projects.json`, matches `Project`/`ProjectHost` interfaces in `projectsRegistry.ts`):
```json
{
  "slug": "my-app",
  "name": "MyApp",
  "tagline": "One sentence pitch",
  "category": "Dev Tool · CLI",
  "status": "live",
  "year": 2026,
  "host": { "kind": "static-path", "path": "/projects/my-app/", "sourceRepo": "github.com/you/repo" },
  "tags": ["Electron", "Free"],

}
```

**B. npm/package metadata** (optional, `src/data/packages.ts`, interface `Package`): `slug, name, npmName, description, install, github, npm, category ('CLI'|'Library'|'Kit'|'App'), scope ('public'|'paid')`.

**C. If you want a marketing/checkout page in Bilko's own SPA (react-route)**: add to `LISTING_TOOLS` in `src/config/tools.ts` (`slug, name, tagline, description, features[], category, status, accent{}, theme{}, loader: () => import('../pages/<X>Page.js')`), plus write the actual `src/pages/<X>Page.tsx` React component (see `SessionManagerPage.tsx` as the worked reference — includes Stripe checkout wiring). This is the higher-friction path since it requires editing the Bilko frontend bundle itself; the contract explicitly says **"New apps default to `static-path`... use `react-route` only when genuinely needed... the trend is the other direction"** (`CLAUDE.md` Rules section).

### 4. Asset hosting — yes, `public/projects/<slug>/`, plus a manifest contract

There **is** a public assets area: `~/Projects/Bilko/public/projects/<slug>/` — one directory per static-path app, containing the app's built `dist/` output verbatim (`index.html`, `assets/`, `manifest.json`, `_headers`). This is served directly by Fastify's `@fastify/static`. No S3/CDN — it's git-committed bytes in the host repo, deployed with the rest of the Bilko app via Render.

Every static-path bundle **must** include a `manifest.json` at its root, schema defined in `mcp-host-server/src/manifest-schema.ts` (Zod) and documented in `docs/host-contract.md` §Manifest contract: `schemaVersion`, `slug`, `version` (semver), `builtAt` (ISO), `gitSha`, `gitBranch`, `hostKit.version`, `golden.path`/`golden.expect` (used by the synthetic monitor), `health.path` (optional), `bundle.sizeBytesGz`, `bundle.fileCount`. Raw JSON must be < 16 KB.

**session-manager already implements this exactly**, in `~/Projects/session-manager/web-remote/app/`:

- `scripts/emit-manifest.mjs` emits `dist/manifest.json` matching the schema (`golden.path: '/projects/session-manager/', golden.expect: 'Session Manager'`)
- `tests/golden.spec.ts` — a Playwright golden-path spec asserting the app shell boots and title contains "Session Manager" (required by the `golden` publish gate)

### 5. Deploy mechanics — git-push-to-deploy, no manual CLI for the base platform

- Bilko itself deploys via Render, auto-deploying from `origin`/`main` (deploy source configured in Render dashboard, no `render.yaml` in-repo).
- **There IS a self-service publish pipeline** for sibling apps — see §6, this is the direct answer to your core question.

### 6. Existing self-service, agent-driven pattern — `mcp-host-server`

This is the most important finding: **Bilko already built exactly the self-service mechanism you're asking to design**, and it's meant to be driven by an agent from the sibling repo, not a human hand-editing Bilko.

`~/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/` (own `package.json`, `bilko-host-mcp`, built with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) exposes an MCP server with 6 tools (`src/server.ts`):

1. **`get_host_contract`** — returns `docs/host-contract.md` verbatim
2. **`list_projects`** — returns the registry (to check slug availability)
3. **`register_static_project`** — writes a new entry into `src/data/standalone-projects.json`, then (if `autoCommit: true`, default) commits and pushes
4. **`unregister_project`** — removes registry entry, optionally `rm -rf public/projects/<slug>/`
5. **`publish_static_project`** — copies a built `dist/` from the sibling repo into `public/projects/<slug>/`, but only after running 5 gates (`mcp-host-server/src/gates/`: `manifest.ts`, `budget.ts` [≤200KB gz default, per-slug override in `app_budgets` table], `golden.ts` [runs `tests/golden.spec.ts` via Playwright in the sibling repo], `a11y.ts` [axe-core scan, zero serious/critical violations], `audit.ts` [`pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high`]). Gates can be individually bypassed with `bypass`/`bypassReason` (audit-logged to a `publish_overrides` Turso table).
6. **`status`** — git status/last-5-commits of the Bilko repo, to verify a publish landed

Wiring: a sibling repo adds a `.mcp.json`:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "bilko-host": { "command": "node", "args": ["/home/bilko/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/dist/server.js"] } } }
```
Claude Code picks it up automatically. Documented flow (`mcp-host-server/README.md` and `docs/host-contract.md` §"Adding from a sibling-repo Claude session"):
```
1. bilko-host__get_host_contract
2. bilko-host__list_projects
3. (build: pnpm/npm build → dist/)
4. bilko-host__register_static_project { slug, name, tagline, category, status, year, sourceRepo, ... }   # first deploy only
5. bilko-host__publish_static_project { slug, distPath, sourceRepoPath }                                    # every deploy
6. bilko-host__status
```

**Important discrepancy to flag for design**: `mcp-host-server/src/server.ts`'s `commitAndPush()` still pushes to **both** `origin` and a `content-grade` remote (lines ~120–144), but Bilko's own `CLAUDE.md` now explicitly states this is **obsolete and wrong** — `content-grade` is "a separate, unrelated project" and Bilko must **never** push there anymore (histories diverged); only `origin`/`main` triggers the real Render deploy. The MCP tool's code hasn't been updated to match. Any automation session-manager builds on top of `bilko-host` should either (a) tolerate/ignore the harmless `content-grade push FAILED` line in the tool's output, or (b) this should be raised/fixed in Bilko first — worth a heads-up to the user since it's a stale landmine in code you'd be depending on.

**Currently, session-manager's own repo does NOT have `bilko-host` wired up** — its `.mcp.json` only registers `session-manager-scheduler`. So today, publishing session-manager's static bundle into Bilko was done by hand (or via an earlier one-off process) rather than through this MCP. The infra to make it self-service already exists; it's just not yet connected on the session-manager side.

### 7. CLAUDE.md / contribution guide conventions

`~/Projects/Bilko/CLAUDE.md` (top-level) states the long-term goal explicitly: *"every app lives in its own sibling repo under `~/Projects/`, built in its own Claude session, and hosted on bilko.run via the static-path contract."* It directs sibling-repo sessions straight to the MCP: *"For Claude sessions working on a sibling app repo (not this one): Use the `bilko-host` MCP... You don't need to edit this repo by hand."* Rules section reiterates: new apps default to `static-path`; push only to `origin`/`main`; static-path fixes belong in the sibling repo, never in the published copy under `public/projects/<slug>/` (the publisher overwrites it on next publish).

`docs/host-contract.md` is the full authoritative spec (441 lines) covering: the three host kinds, what the host provides per kind, what an app must implement, URL canonicalization rules, the add/remove checklists, the manifest contract, the 5-gate publish pipeline, synthetic monitoring (6h headless-Chromium checks against `manifest.golden.path`), security headers/CSP applied even to static-path siblings, and telemetry (`@bilkobibitkov/host-kit`'s `initTelemetry`).

- `src/data/packages.ts` also lists `session-manager` as an npm `Package` (category `'App'`, npmName `claude-code-session-manager`) — this feeds the npm/github/install links onto the hub card via `projectsView.ts`'s `pkgBySlug` merge.

So: **not hand-coded HTML, and not a "full deployed service" in Bilko's own infra** — it's registry JSON/TS entries that the Bilko frontend reads to render cards/pages, PLUS a static asset drop for the actual bytes.

### 3. Exact data shape needed

**A. Static-path registry entry** (`src/data/standalone-projects.json`, matches `Project`/`ProjectHost` interfaces in `projectsRegistry.ts`):
```json
{
  "slug": "my-app",
  "name": "MyApp",
  "tagline": "One sentence pitch",
  "category": "Dev Tool · CLI",
  "status": "live",
  "year": 2026,
  "host": { "kind": "static-path", "path": "/projects/my-app/", "sourceRepo": "github.com/you/repo" },
  "tags": ["Electron", "Free"],
  "thumbnail": "optional cover image path"
}
```

**B. npm/package metadata** (optional, `src/data/packages.ts`, interface `Package`): `slug, name, npmName, description, install, github, npm, category ('CLI'|'Library'|'Kit'|'App'), scope ('public'|'paid')`.

**C. If you want a marketing/checkout page in Bilko's own SPA (react-route)**: add to `LISTING_TOOLS` in `src/config/tools.ts` (`slug, name, tagline, description, features[], category, status, accent{}, theme{}, loader: () => import('../pages/<X>Page.js')`), plus write the actual `src/pages/<X>Page.tsx` React component (see `SessionManagerPage.tsx` as the worked reference — includes Stripe checkout wiring). This is the higher-friction path since it requires editing the Bilko frontend bundle itself; the contract explicitly says **"New apps default to `static-path`... use `react-route` only when genuinely needed... the trend is the other direction"** (`CLAUDE.md` Rules section).

**D. Public "buy/checkout config"**: lives server-side in `server/routes/stripe.ts` and product-key constants (`PRODUCT_KEYS.SESSION_MANAGER` used in `tools.ts`) — this is Bilko-internal, only relevant for the `react-route` checkout page pattern, not needed for a plain static-path listing.

### 4. Asset hosting — yes, `public/projects/<slug>/`, plus a manifest contract

There **is** a public assets area: `~/Projects/Bilko/public/projects/<slug>/` — one directory per static-path app, containing the app's built `dist/` output verbatim (`index.html`, `assets/`, `manifest.json`, `_headers`). This is served directly by Fastify's `@fastify/static`. No S3/CDN — it's git-committed bytes in the host repo, deployed with the rest of the Bilko app via Render.

Every static-path bundle **must** include a `manifest.json` at its root, schema defined in `mcp-host-server/src/manifest-schema.ts` (Zod) and documented in `docs/host-contract.md` §Manifest contract: `schemaVersion`, `slug`, `version` (semver), `builtAt` (ISO), `gitSha`, `gitBranch`, `hostKit.version`, `golden.path`/`golden.expect` (used by the synthetic monitor), `health.path` (optional), `bundle.sizeBytesGz`, `bundle.fileCount`. Raw JSON must be < 16 KB.

**session-manager already implements this exactly**, in `~/Projects/session-manager/web-remote/app/`:
- `vite.config.ts` sets `base: '/projects/session-manager/'` (host-contract compliant)
- `scripts/emit-manifest.mjs` emits `dist/manifest.json` matching the schema (`golden.path: '/projects/session-manager/', golden.expect: 'Session Manager'`)
- `tests/golden.spec.ts` — a Playwright golden-path spec asserting the app shell boots and title contains "Session Manager" (required by the `golden` publish gate)
- `package.json` build script: `"build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build && node scripts/emit-manifest.mjs"`
- The currently-published copy is already sitting in Bilko at `public/projects/session-manager/` (index.html, assets/, manifest.json — last built `2026-07-21`, version `0.1.0`, gitSha `69c1d7a`).

Note: session-manager's `web-remote/app` also has an **independent `render.yaml`** targeting a separate Render *static site* deploy at `session-manager.bilko.run` (a subdomain, not `bilko.run/projects/...`) — this is a second, parallel deploy path unrelated to the Bilko-repo publish flow; worth clarifying with the user which one "Host on Bilko.run" should target (the `/projects/session-manager/` path inside the main bilko-run Render service, vs. the separate `session-manager.bilko.run` static site).

### 5. Deploy mechanics — git-push-to-deploy, no manual CLI for the base platform

- Bilko itself deploys via Render, auto-deploying from `origin`/`main` (deploy source configured in Render dashboard, no `render.yaml` in-repo).
- **There IS a self-service publish pipeline** for sibling apps — see §6, this is the direct answer to your core question.

### 6. Existing self-service, agent-driven pattern — `mcp-host-server`

This is the most important finding: **Bilko already built exactly the self-service mechanism you're asking to design**, and it's meant to be driven by an agent from the sibling repo, not a human hand-editing Bilko.

`~/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/` (own `package.json`, `bilko-host-mcp`, built with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) exposes an MCP server with 6 tools (`src/server.ts`):

1. **`get_host_contract`** — returns `docs/host-contract.md` verbatim
2. **`list_projects`** — returns the registry (to check slug availability)
3. **`register_static_project`** — writes a new entry into `src/data/standalone-projects.json`, then (if `autoCommit: true`, default) commits and pushes
4. **`unregister_project`** — removes registry entry, optionally `rm -rf public/projects/<slug>/`
5. **`publish_static_project`** — copies a built `dist/` from the sibling repo into `public/projects/<slug>/`, but only after running 5 gates (`mcp-host-server/src/gates/`: `manifest.ts`, `budget.ts` [≤200KB gz default, per-slug override in `app_budgets` table], `golden.ts` [runs `tests/golden.spec.ts` via Playwright in the sibling repo], `a11y.ts` [axe-core scan, zero serious/critical violations], `audit.ts` [`pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high`]). Gates can be individually bypassed with `bypass`/`bypassReason` (audit-logged to a `publish_overrides` Turso table).
6. **`status`** — git status/last-5-commits of the Bilko repo, to verify a publish landed

Wiring: a sibling repo adds a `.mcp.json`:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "bilko-host": { "command": "node", "args": ["/home/bilko/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/dist/server.js"] } } }
```
Claude Code picks it up automatically. Documented flow (`mcp-host-server/README.md` and `docs/host-contract.md` §"Adding from a sibling-repo Claude session"):
```
1. bilko-host__get_host_contract
2. bilko-host__list_projects
3. (build: pnpm/npm build → dist/)
4. bilko-host__register_static_project { slug, name, tagline, category, status, year, sourceRepo, ... }   # first deploy only
5. bilko-host__publish_static_project { slug, distPath, sourceRepoPath }                                    # every deploy
6. bilko-host__status
```

**Important discrepancy to flag for design**: `mcp-host-server/src/server.ts`'s `commitAndPush()` still pushes to **both** `origin` and a `content-grade` remote (lines ~120–144), but Bilko's own `CLAUDE.md` now explicitly states this is **obsolete and wrong** — `content-grade` is "a separate, unrelated project" and Bilko must **never** push there anymore (histories diverged); only `origin`/`main` triggers the real Render deploy. The MCP tool's code hasn't been updated to match. Any automation session-manager builds on top of `bilko-host` should either (a) tolerate/ignore the harmless `content-grade push FAILED` line in the tool's output, or (b) this should be raised/fixed in Bilko first — worth a heads-up to the user since it's a stale landmine in code you'd be depending on.

**Currently, session-manager's own repo does NOT have `bilko-host` wired up** — its `.mcp.json` only registers `session-manager-scheduler`. So today, publishing session-manager's static bundle into Bilko was done by hand (or via an earlier one-off process) rather than through this MCP. The infra to make it self-service already exists; it's just not yet connected on the session-manager side.

### 7. CLAUDE.md / contribution guide conventions

`~/Projects/Bilko/CLAUDE.md` (top-level) states the long-term goal explicitly: *"every app lives in its own sibling repo under `~/Projects/`, built in its own Claude session, and hosted on bilko.run via the static-path contract."* It directs sibling-repo sessions straight to the MCP: *"For Claude sessions working on a sibling app repo (not this one): Use the `bilko-host` MCP... You don't need to edit this repo by hand."* Rules section reiterates: new apps default to `static-path`; push only to `origin`/`main`; static-path fixes belong in the sibling repo, never in the published copy under `public/projects/<slug>/` (the publisher overwrites it on next publish).

`docs/host-contract.md` is the full authoritative spec (441 lines) covering: the three host kinds, what the host provides per kind, what an app must implement, URL canonicalization rules, the add/remove checklists, the manifest contract, the 5-gate publish pipeline, synthetic monitoring (6h headless-Chromium checks against `manifest.golden.path`), security headers/CSP applied even to static-path siblings, and telemetry (`@bilkobibitkov/host-kit`'s `initTelemetry`).

---

## Mechanically: what it would take for session-manager to self-publish to bilko.run

Given all of the above, session-manager is **almost fully positioned already** — the missing piece is purely the connective wiring, not new Bilko infrastructure:

1. **Add `.mcp.json` entry** in `~/Projects/session-manager/` (or specifically in `web-remote/app/` if that's the intended publish unit) pointing at `/home/bilko/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/dist/server.js` (needs `pnpm install && pnpm build` run once inside `mcp-host-server/` if `dist/server.js` isn't already built — verify).
2. **Build the static bundle**: `cd web-remote/app && npm run build` (already runs `vite build` + `emit-manifest.mjs` — no changes needed, this pipeline is complete and host-contract-compliant today).
3. **Register once** (idempotent-safe — errors if slug taken, which it is, so this step is effectively "confirm already registered" via `bilko-host__list_projects`, or `unregister_project` + re-`register_static_project` if metadata needs to change).
4. **Publish on every release**: `bilko-host__publish_static_project { slug: 'session-manager', distPath: '<abs>/web-remote/app/dist', sourceRepoPath: '<abs>/web-remote/app' }` — this runs the 5 gates (manifest/budget/golden/a11y/audit) using session-manager's own `tests/golden.spec.ts` and `manifest.json`, then copies bytes into Bilko's `public/projects/session-manager/`, commits, and pushes to `origin` (triggering Render redeploy).
5. **Verify** via `bilko-host__status` and/or hitting `bilko.run/projects/session-manager/`.

This is a `develop`-skill-sized, agent-drivable PRD: wire the MCP, then have the agent run steps 2–5 as part of a release/publish flow (potentially hooked into the existing `session-manager-dev:builder` skill's publish step, or as a new step after npm publish). No human hand-edit of the Bilko repo is required for this path — that's the entire point of `mcp-host-server`. The one open design decision to resolve with the user is which of the two live deploy targets "Host on Bilko.run" should mean: (a) the `bilko.run/projects/session-manager/` path via this MCP pipeline (recommended — it's the documented, gated, agent-native path), or (b) the separate `session-manager.bilko.run` Render static site defined by `web-remote/app/render.yaml` (a parallel, ungated, direct-git-push Render deploy with no relation to the Bilko monorepo's registry/gates at all).</result>

bilko.run is a **host platform**, not a single product. It hosts many independent "apps" — each with its own product, its own scoring engine, its own UX. Some apps live in this repo; some live in their own repos and are dropped in as static assets; some live on other domains.

This document defines the contract: what the host provides, what an app must implement, and how to add a new app.

## The three host kinds

Every app declares one host kind in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`:

| Kind | When to use | Path | Coupling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | App needs the shared auth/credit/component kit and is small enough to live alongside the others | `/products/<slug>` | Tight — same Vite build, same Fastify server |
| `static-path` | App is built in its own repo (often its own Claude session) and just needs a URL on bilko.run | `/projects/<slug>/` | Loose — host serves prebuilt static assets, no shared runtime |
| `external-url` | App lives on another domain or subdomain | `https://<host>/...` | None — host only links to it |

Default to `static-path` for new apps unless they need shared auth or credits. `react-route` is for the AI-tool family that already shares the kit.

## What the host provides

These are the OS services. Apps use them; they should not reimplement.

### To every app, regardless of host kind

- **Brand chrome.** Header, footer, blog, /pricing, /privacy, /terms, /admin, ⌘K command palette.
- **Portfolio listing.** Anything in `projectsRegistry.ts` shows up on `/`, `/products`, and ⌘K automatically. No manual wiring.
- **Domain.** `bilko.run/<your-path>`.

### To `react-route` apps additionally

- **Auth: Clerk.** Available via `useUser()` and `useAuth()` from `@clerk/clerk-react`. Server-side: `requireAuth(req, reply)` from `server/clerk.ts` returns the Clerk email or 401s.
- **Credits: token wallet.** Spend via `deductToken(email)` and check via `getTokenBalance(email)` from `server/services/tokens.ts`. Free users get a starter grant via `grantFreeTokens(email)`.
- **Payments: Stripe.** Subscription state via `getActiveSubscriptionLive(email)`; one-time purchases via `hasPurchased(email, productKey)`. Both from `server/services/stripe.ts`.
- **Rate limiting.** `checkRateLimit(ipHash, endpoint, email?, productKey?)` from `server/routes/tools/_shared.ts` — handles free-tier daily caps, paid-tier caps, pro-skip.
- **Page-view analytics.** `usePageView()` hook fires once per route mount.
- **Component kit.** `src/components/tool-page/` — `ToolHero`, `ScoreCard`, `SectionBreakdown`, `CompareLayout`, `Rewrites`, `CrossPromo`, `colors.ts`. Use these instead of building custom UI for grade/score displays.
- **Tool API hook.** `useToolApi()` in `src/hooks/` wraps auth, submit, compare, generate, error/loading/token state.
- **Gemini.** `askGemini(prompt, opts)` from `server/gemini.ts`. Use `parseJsonResponse` (re-exported as `parseResult` in `_shared.ts`) for JSON outputs.
- **Database.** Turso/libSQL via `dbGet/dbAll/dbRun/dbTransaction` from `server/db.ts`. Falls back to local SQLite in dev. All SQL parameterized.

### To `static-path` and `external-url` apps additionally

- **Nothing.** That's the point. Bring your own runtime, your own auth (or none), your own everything. Host just serves the bytes.

## What an app must implement

### Every app

A single entry in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`:

```ts
{
  slug: 'my-app',
  name: 'MyApp',
  tagline: 'One sentence: what is this and who is it for.',
  category: 'AI Tool · Content', // or 'Game', 'Data', etc.
  status: 'live', // | 'cooking' | 'archived'
  year: 2026,
  host: { kind: 'static-path', path: '/projects/my-app/' },
  tags: ['Browser', 'Free'],
}
```

### `react-route` apps additionally

- A `<MyAppPage />` React component in `src/pages/MyAppPage.tsx`.
- An entry in `src/config/tools.ts` (`LISTING_TOOLS`) with the slug, tagline, category, and a `loader` (the React.lazy import).
- Backend routes in `server/routes/tools/<my-app>.ts` exporting `registerMyAppRoutes(app)`, registered in `server/routes/tools/index.ts`.
- For paid features, deduct credits via `deductToken(email)` after a successful response; for free-tier, gate via `checkRateLimit()` and increment via `incrementUsage()`.

### `static-path` apps additionally

- A standalone build that emits to `dist/` in your own repo.
- A sync step (manual or scripted) that copies `dist/` into `public/projects/<slug>/` of this repo.
- The build's `index.html` must use relative or `/projects/<slug>/`-prefixed asset paths (Vite: set `base: '/projects/<slug>/'`).
- No assumption about parent-page layout — your bundle owns the entire page.
- **A `manifest.json` at the bundle root** (`dist/manifest.json`) — see "Manifest contract" below. `publish_static_project` refuses bundles without one.

### `external-url` apps

- Just the URL.

## URL canonicalization

- `/products/<slug>` is the canonical path for every `react-route` app.
- `/projects/<slug>` redirects (301-style SPA `Navigate replace`) to `/products/<slug>`.
- `/app/<old-slug>` redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>` per the `APP_TO_PRODUCT` map in `src/App.tsx`. (Pre-refactor compatibility.)
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, `static-path`) does **not** redirect — it's a different host kind serving different bytes.

## Adding a new app — checklist

1. Decide the host kind. Default `static-path` unless you need shared auth/credits → `react-route`.
2. Build it.
   - `react-route`: page + route entry + per-tool server file.

4. Run `pnpm test && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm exec vite build` — all must pass.
5. Commit and push to both remotes (`origin` and `content-grade`). Render auto-deploys.
6. Verify the project shows up on `/`, `/products`, and in ⌘K.

per-project surface that turns an already-generated [Project Page](project-pages-pipeline.md)
(the `marketing` lens) into a real listing on bilko.run, with a one-click
**Publish** action. This is the single source of truth for the `bilko-host`
OWNERS namespace, the `bilko-host-publisher` Epic tag + local agent, and the
`HostBilko.tsx` tab — edit here, not in any of those, when the design

## Bilko.run already has a self-service publish pipeline — use it, don't rebuild it

`~/Projects/Bilko` (the sibling repo backing bilko.run) is a host **platform**:
apps declare a `host.kind` in its project registry —
`react-route` (tightly coupled, shares Bilko's own Vite bundle/Fastify
server/auth/Stripe), `static-path` (loose — host just serves prebuilt static
bytes at `/projects/<slug>/`, **the default for new/sibling apps**), or
`external-url` (just a link). The full contract is
`~/Projects/Bilko/docs/host-contract.md`.

Critically, Bilko already ships **`mcp-host-server`**
(`~/Projects/Bilko/mcp-host-server/`, built, `dist/server.js` present) — an
MCP server explicitly designed for sibling-repo Claude sessions to publish
themselves **without hand-editing the Bilko repo**:

| MCP tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `get_host_contract` | returns `docs/host-contract.md` verbatim — ground the agent on current rules, never hardcode them |
| `list_projects` | check whether a slug is already registered |
| `register_static_project` | writes the registry entry (first publish only) |
| `publish_static_project` | copies a built `dist/` into `public/projects/<slug>/`, gated by 5 checks (manifest schema, size budget, a Playwright "golden path" spec, an a11y scan, `pnpm audit`), commits + pushes `origin/main` (Render auto-deploys) |
| `unregister_project` | remove a listing |
| `status` | git status / last commits, to confirm a publish landed |

  feature: { bg: 'bg-sage/20', text: 'text-sage', border: true, label: 'Feature' },
  bug: { bg: 'bg-accent/15', text: 'text-accent', border: true, label: 'Bug' },
  discussion: { bg: 'bg-butter/25', text: 'text-fg-dim', border: true, label: 'Discussion' },
  build: { bg: 'bg-hive-teal/20', text: 'text-hive-teal', border: true, label: 'Build' },
  'project-home-builder': { bg: 'bg-honey/20', text: 'text-honey-dark', border: true, label: 'Project Home Builder' },
}

export function ticketTagTone(tag: TicketTag) {
  return TAG_TONE[tag]
}

/**
 * A 'discussion' ticket is an explicit statement of intent: the user wants an
 * interactive research conversation, not decomposition into scheduled PRDs.
 * dequeueNext() short-circuits the classifier on this, the same way it does
 * for external-origin tickets — different reason, same guarantee that
 * dispatchToPrd() is unreachable.
 */
export function isDiscussionTag(tag: TicketTag | undefined): boolean {
  return tag === 'discussion'
}

/**
 * FIFO order for the chat queue panel: past tickets (oldest first), then the
 * one currently in flight, then anything still waiting behind it — except
 * any 'needs-input' ticket, which is pinned to the very top so a stalled
 * question can never scroll out of view behind newer queued/history tickets.
 */
export function mergeTicketsForDisplay(
  ticketHistory: PromptTicket[],
  activeTicket: PromptTicket | null | undefined,
  queue: PromptTicket[],
): PromptTicket[] {
  const all = [...ticketHistory, ...(activeTicket ? [activeTicket] : []), ...queue]
  const needsInput = all.filter((t) => t.status === 'needs-input')
  const rest = all.filter((t) => t.status !== 'needs-input')
  return [...needsInput, ...rest]
}

import type { NavKey } from '../LeftNav'
import { useSessions } from '../../state/sessions'

// group below Configure so users see them as workflow surfaces (not
// configuration). Same NavKey type as Workspace/Configure rows.
type ToolKey = Extract<NavKey,

  key: ToolKey

function toolItems(items: NavGroupItem[]): ToolItem[] {
  return items
    .filter((item): item is NavGroupItem & { key: ToolKey } => item.group === 'Tools')
    .map(({ key, label, icon, hint }) => ({ key, label, icon, hint }))

const WIDTH_MIN = 180
const WIDTH_MAX = 480
const WIDTH_DEFAULT = 252
function loadWidth(): number {
  try {
    const v = parseInt(localStorage.getItem(WIDTH_KEY) ?? '', 10)
    if (Number.isFinite(v)) return Math.min(WIDTH_MAX, Math.max(WIDTH_MIN, v))
  } catch { /* ignore */ }
  return WIDTH_DEFAULT
}

const SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED_KEY = 'sm.almanac.sidebarCollapsed'

function loadCollapsedRail(): boolean {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED_KEY) === '1'
  } catch { /* ignore */ }
  return false
}
